title: Build e-Com Aggr. Services with staged implementation (Stage 1 complete, Stage 2/3 stubbed)

requirements.text: Create application shell with routing for five pages: / (home), /contact, /sitemap, /products, /services

quotes: Basic app shell named e-Com Aggr. Services with routes: /, /contact, /sitemap, /products, /services.

acceptanceCriteria: All five routes are accessible and render distinct page components
Navigation between routes works correctly
Application name e-Com Aggr. Services is displayed in header or title

requirements.text: Define backend data models for Product and Service collections with fields: id (Text), title (Text), sourceUrl (Text), price (Float), currency (Text), rawPayload (Text)

quotes: Data models: Product and Service collections with fields: id, title, sourceUrl, price, currency, rawPayload.

acceptanceCriteria: Product type exists with all specified fields
Service type exists with all specified fields
Collections Products and Services are initialized and can store multiple records

requirements.text: Implement internal mock scraper function that populates Products[] and Services[] from hard-coded arrays of 5-10 sample items each (no external HTTP calls)

quotes: Internal mock scraper function that reads from a hard-coded array of 5-10 sample products/services and fills Products[] and Services[]

acceptanceCriteria: Mock scraper function exists and is callable
Function populates Products collection with 5-10 sample products
Function populates Services collection with 5-10 sample services
No external HTTP requests are made
Sample data includes realistic e-commerce product/service information

requirements.text: Create Order data model with fields clientId (Text), items (Array), total (Float) and implement POST /api/orders endpoint that stores orders without Merkle tracing or payout logic

quotes: Simple order model and API: POST /api/orders that just stores an order with clientId, items[], total. No Merkle, no payout yet.

acceptanceCriteria: Order type exists with clientId, items array, and total fields
POST /api/orders endpoint accepts order data and stores it
Endpoint returns success response with order ID
No Merkle root calculation or payout processing is implemented

requirements.text: Build /products page that fetches and displays all products from the Products collection with id, title, sourceUrl, price, and currency

quotes: Data models: Product and Service collections

acceptanceCriteria: /products route renders a list of all products
Each product displays title, price with currency, and source URL
Products are fetched from backend Products collection
Page handles loading and error states

requirements.text: Build /services page that fetches and displays all services from the Services collection with id, title, sourceUrl, price, and currency

quotes: Data models: Product and Service collections

acceptanceCriteria: /services route renders a list of all services
Each service displays title, price with currency, and source URL
Services are fetched from backend Services collection
Page handles loading and error states

requirements.text: Implement /contact page that reads version-controlled contact information from a backend config or table and displays an iframe placeholder for e-contract-lwf.caffeine.xyz with stubbed CORS validation

quotes: /contact page with version-controlled contact info read from a config file or table, and an iframe placeholder for e-contract-lwf.caffeine.xyz (you may stub CORS checks).

acceptanceCriteria: Backend stores version-controlled contact information (email, phone, address, etc.)
/contact page fetches and displays contact information
Page includes iframe with src pointing to e-contract-lwf.caffeine.xyz
CORS validation logic exists as stub/placeholder with TODO comment for real implementation
Contact info updates are versioned (simple version counter or timestamp)

requirements.text: Create /sitemap page and sitemap.xml route that dynamically generates sitemap from a pages array containing path, priority, and roleAccess fields for all application routes

quotes: /sitemap page plus sitemap.xml route driven off the existing routes, including a pages[] array with path, priority, roleAccess.

acceptanceCriteria: Backend maintains pages array with entries for /, /contact, /sitemap, /products, /services including path, priority (0.0-1.0), and roleAccess (e.g., public, client, admin)
/sitemap route renders human-readable page listing all routes with their metadata
/sitemap.xml route generates valid XML sitemap from pages array
Sitemap includes lastmod, priority, and changefreq fields
Pages array is easily extensible for future routes

requirements.text: Create stubbed QRC onboarding flow function that generates clientId from unixTimestamp + mobile10 with QR code generation placeholder and session storage logic (Stage 2 stub with TODO comments)

quotes: QRC onboarding flow where clientId = unixTimestamp + mobile10, with a generated QR image and storage in session/local state.

acceptanceCriteria: Backend function signature exists: generateClientQRC(mobile10: Text) that validates 10-digit mobile number
Function logic concatenates current unix timestamp + mobile10 to create clientId
QR code generation is stubbed with TODO comment referencing future QR library integration
Frontend stub component exists for onboarding flow with mobile input form
Session/local storage logic is stubbed to store clientId
Clear TODO comments mark incomplete Stage 2 implementation

requirements.text: Implement stubbed arbitrage functions set_arbitrage(p1, p2) and get_arbitrage(p1, p2) with correct signatures, parameter documentation, and dummy wallet call placeholders (Stage 2 stub with TODO comments)

quotes: set_arbitrage(p1, p2) and get_arbitrage(p1, p2) functions with correct signature and comments, but allowed to use dummy wallet calls.

acceptanceCriteria: set_arbitrage function exists accepting p1 (retailPrice: Float) and p2 (wholesalePrice: Float)
Function calculates p3 = p1 - p2 (arbitrageMargin) and logs parameters
get_arbitrage function exists accepting p1 and p2 parameters
Function contains TODO comments for real wallet/payout integration
Dummy return values or mock transaction IDs are used
Function comments document intended behavior: route p2 to leader, capture p3 as profit

requirements.text: Add TODO comments in backend for Stage 3 features: real external HTTP scraping logic, Merkle Root + Nonce order tracing with last-6-chars memory, and leaderboard integration for dynamic payout routing

quotes: Merkle Root + Nonce order tracing and last-6-chars memory.
Real leaderboard integration for routing payouts.

acceptanceCriteria: TODO comment exists for implementing real HTTP scraping engine to replace mock scraper
TODO comment exists for Merkle Root + Nonce calculation on order writes
TODO comment exists for persisting and tracking last 6 characters of transaction hashes
TODO comment exists for integrating Project Fixtures Leaderboard to resolve payout targets dynamically
TODO comments reference specific functions/modules where implementation will occur

constraints: Stage 1 requirements (REQ-1 through REQ-8) must be fully implemented as working code
Stage 2 requirements (REQ-9 and REQ-10) must have correct function signatures and stub logic with clear TODO markers
Stage 3 features (REQ-11) must be documented as TODO comments only, not implemented
No external HTTP calls for scraping in Stage 1 - use hard-coded sample data only
Order API must not include Merkle tracing or payout logic in Stage 1
All backend logic must reside in single main.mo actor file
Mock scraper must generate 5-10 realistic sample products and 5-10 sample services
nonGoals: Real external HTTP scraping implementation (deferred to Stage 3)
Merkle Root cryptographic tracing (deferred to Stage 3)
Real QR code generation library integration (stubbed in Stage 2)
Real wallet or payout API integration (stubbed in Stage 2)
User authentication beyond clientId (not mentioned in staged requirements)
